newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland complains about British nuclear facility.
newsitem.headline: Ireland complains about British nuclear facility.

text.p: Ireland on Friday called in the British ambassador to voice oncern over Britain's nuclear activities after two incidents within 24 hours at the Sellafield nuclear complex in Cumbria on the other side of the Irish sea.

Emmet Stagg, Irish minister with responsibility for nuclear safety, held an hour-long meeting with ambassador Veronica Sutherland to discuss the latest incidents at Sellafield, which is operated by state-owned British Nuclear Fuels (BNFL).

"The minister reiterated the deep-felt concern of the government and Irish people over the constant system failures and incidents at British Nuclear Facilities and, in particular, at the Sellafield Nuclear Reprocessing Plant," an Irish government spokeswoman said.
Stagg also stressed the government's opposition to a proposed nuclear dump near Sellafield and asked Sutherland to convey these concerns to the British government.
On Sunday, six BNFL workers were slightly contaminated at the Magnox fuel reprocessing plant. This was followed by the spillage of radioactive liquid from a storage tank complex on Monday.
Stagg said he was outraged by the latest incidents.
"I call it a disgrace. The frequency of this litany of leaks, mishaps and incidences surrounding the Sellafield complex has totally shattered public confidence in the complex," he said on Wednesday.
BNFL is investigating the causes of the incidents, which they said posed no danger to the workforce, general public or the environment.
Ireland is also concerned about plans by state-controlled company Nirex to build an underground laboratory to explore whether a site near Sellafield would make a safe underground dump for waste.
A scientists' report earlier this week indicated that radioactive material from the proposed underground waste storage site at Sellafield could seep into the Irish Sea.

"The people of Ireland are deeply concerned and fearful of this latest proposed British nuclear facility," Stagg wrote in a letter to his British counterpart, Secretary of State for the Environment, John Gummer. "We urge you not to proceed with Nirex."
